Subject: Offer proposal and leveling for Jordan Miles (L5 manager vs L5 IC)

Hi all,

Quick thread to get alignment before Marissa extends. We have a strong candidate, Jordan Miles (resume attached). Jordan has 4 years of IC experience + 3 years leading a small analytics team (4 headcount) at their last role. They explicitly want a manager role and would prefer scope over title, but compensation expectations are around $160–180k base + equity.

Options on the table:
- L5 IC (manager track) — base $155–165k, equity 0.3–0.45%, small sign-on
- L5 Manager — base $165–175k, equity 0.45–0.6%, sign-on $10–20k
- Stretch to L6 (not recommended without bigger scope) — would push base >$190k and require exec sign-off and HC reprioritization

Attached: jordan_miles_resume.pdf, comp_model_v3.xlsx (working comps).

Asks:
1) Level recommendation (L5 IC vs L5 Manager) — please call out risks for promotion path vs title inflation.
2) Compensation guidance (base, equity, sign-on cap).
3) Any headcount/finance blockers (Mina), or DPE approval required for sign-on > $20k?

Goal: finalize and extend by EOD Friday (2026-09-03).

Thanks,
Tessa

Tessa — thanks for the summary. My read: give Jordan the manager title. They've led a team before and wants scope; promoting into a manager role will increase acceptance and retention. I think L5 Manager is appropriate.

Comp recommendation (market + internal parity):
- Base: $170,000
- Equity: 0.5%
- Sign-on: up to $15,000 (one-time)

Risks:
- Slight inflation vs other recent L5 IC hires — prepare a documented leveling justification (brief bullet list of leadership scope).
- If we push to L6, we need to add at least 30% to base and equity which I don't support here.

Happy to discuss but I'm comfortable with L5 Manager at the numbers above.

Thanks, Tessa. I agree Jordan is strong and the leadership experience is real — however, two cautions:

1) Level inflation: we recently promoted two L5 ICs with leadership coaching but kept titles IC to preserve calibration for L6. If we push manager now we need to ensure managerial expectations (people management, 1:1s, PIPs, performance calibration) are clearly documented in the role profile.
2) Comp parity: current L5 Manager band at Redwood is guidance base $160–180k, equity 0.4–0.6%. We should sit in the middle to avoid pressure on adjacent teams.

My recommendation: L5 Manager is OK if we attach a 6-month manager ramp plan and a clear success criteria doc. Base at $168k, equity 0.5%, sign-on capped at $10k unless DPE approves higher. Please add the ramp plan to the offer packet.

-Laura

Redwood Inference
